title: Barefoot at the piano (Barfuß am Klavier)
summary: A quiet break-up song from Cologne: simple words, clever wordplay, and the way Germans really drop their endings when they speak.
goals: Hear spoken German: ich sitz, ich hab, war'n
Catch the two puns: gemeinsam einsam, um zu lieben, lieber
Learn a false friend: wunderlich is not 'wonderful'

sections.title: About this song
sections.text:
**AnnenMayKantereit** are a band from Cologne. Three school friends started them in 2011 as street musicians, and the name is simply their three surnames: Annen, May, Kantereit. The singer, Henning May, is known for his rough, raspy voice.

'Barfuß am Klavier' is on their first album, **Alles nix Konkretes** (March 2016), which went to number 1 in Germany.

Why it's good for you: the words are simple (du, ich, sitzen, träumen, lieben), the first chorus line comes back four times, and the song is full of real spoken German. The singer is sitting barefoot at the piano, singing about someone who is gone.

Germans drop the -e of the ich form all the time when they speak: [[ich hab]], [[ich geh]], [[ich komm]]. When you write, keep it: [[ich habe]]. The verb endings you learned in Unit 1 are still there, just swallowed.

items.de: Und ich sitz schon wieder barfuß am Klavier
items.en: And here I am again, sitting barefoot at the piano
items.note: schon wieder = (yet) again, often a little annoyed

items.de: Ich träume Liebeslieder und sing dabei von dir
items.en: I dream love songs and sing about you while I'm at it
items.note: dabei = at the same time, while doing that

sections.title: What's going on in the chorus
sections.text:
- [[schon wieder]]: 'already again', i.e. yet again. You'll hear it everywhere: [[Der Zug ist schon wieder zu spät.]] (The train is late again.)
- [[am Klavier]]: [[am]] = [[an dem]], 'at the'. You sit **at** a piano, a desk or a table: [[am Tisch]]. Unit 6 teaches it properly.
- [[Liebeslieder]]: [[die Liebe]] (love) + [[das Lied]] (song), with an -s- in between as glue. The plural of [[das Lied]] is [[die Lieder]], so [[die Liebeslieder]].
- [[Ich träume Liebeslieder]] is poetic. Normally you dream **of** something: [[Ich träume von dir.]] Here he 'dreams up' love songs.
- [[von dir singen]] = to sing about you. [[von]] also means 'about' with singen, träumen and erzählen (to tell).

items.de: Du und ich, wir waren wunderlich
items.en: You and I, we were strange

items.de: Du und ich, wir war'n mal wir. Und sind jetzt nichts
items.en: You and I, we used to be an 'us'. And now we're nothing
items.note: mal = once, at one time (short for einmal)
No verb at all, and it doesn't need one.

sections.text: False friend: [[wunderlich]] means strange or odd, a bit old-fashioned. 'Wonderful' is [[wunderbar]] or [[toll]]. Say [[Das ist wunderbar!]] to a host, never [[Das ist wunderlich!]]

items.de: Ich hab mit dir gemeinsam einsam rumgesessen und geschwiegen
items.en: Together with you, I sat around lonely and kept quiet
items.note: gemeinsam (together) and einsam (lonely) rhyme: together, but alone.

items.de: Also sitz ich, um zu lieben, lieber barfuß am Klavier
items.en: So, to do my loving, I'd rather sit barefoot at the piano
items.note: lieben (to love) and lieber (rather) sound almost the same.

sections.title: How the puns work
sections.text:
- [[gemeinsam einsam]]: two people together and still lonely. [[gemeinsam]] = together, shared ([[Wir essen gemeinsam.]]). [[einsam]] = lonely.
- [[rumgesessen und geschwiegen]]: this is the Perfekt, the spoken past (Unit 5): [[ich hab ... gesessen]] (I sat), [[... geschwiegen]] (kept silent). [[rum-]] is spoken for [[herum-]] (around).
- [[um zu lieben, lieber]]: [[um ... zu]] + verb = in order to ([[um zu lieben]] = in order to love). Then [[lieber]] = rather, preferably, from [[gern, lieber, am liebsten]] (Unit 4). He'd rather love through songs than in real life.
- [[Also sitz ich]]: after [[also]] (so), the verb comes straight after, before [[ich]]: verb in second place (Unit 1). And remember [[also]] means 'so', not 'also'.

items.de: Du nackt im Bett - und ich barfuß am Klavier
items.en: You naked in bed, and me barefoot at the piano

sections.title: Words worth keeping
rows: to be silent, to say nothing

sections.title: How to use it
sections.text:
1. Listen once with the link above, just for the feeling.
2. Read the chorus here and listen again: it keeps coming back, so by the end you can sing along.
3. Shadow one line: pause the video after a line and repeat it in the same rhythm. [[Und ich sitz schon wieder barfuß am Klavier]] is a perfect first one.
4. Notice every dropped -e: sitz, träum, sing, hab.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: And here I am again, sitting barefoot at the piano.
items.text: Und ich sitz schon ___ barfuß am Klavier

items.question: Which word means 'strange, odd'?
items.explanation: wunderlich = strange, odd. wunderbar = wonderful; einsam = lonely.

items.question: In the song, 'ich sitz' is spoken German. How do you write it?
items.explanation: The ich form ends in -e: ich sitze. In speech the -e often disappears: ich sitz.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap with the word that rhymes with 'gemeinsam': together, but lonely.
items.text: Ich hab mit dir gemeinsam ___ rumgesessen
items.explanation: gemeinsam (together) + einsam (lonely): the pun of the song.

items.prompt: You and I, we were strange.
answers: Du und ich wir waren wunderlich
items.explanation: Du und ich, wir waren wunderlich: the verb (waren) comes second in 'wir waren wunderlich'.
